```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))   # analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations -> analysis
os.chdir("..")                                # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import laplacelib as R
import pip_agreement as P

comp, fits, feat = P.load()
cn, fn = comp.filter(~pl.col("null")), fits.filter(~pl.col("null"))
tf = P.tail_frame(fn)   # fits with max |dPIP| > 0.1, attributed to a component pair
```

Every arm is compared with CAVI-Q2 on the same replicate. For single effect $l$,
$\alpha_l$ is the posterior over which feature carries the effect: $\alpha_l =
\text{softmax}(\log \text{BF}_l)$ under the uniform prior. Three distances between CAVI-Q2's
$\alpha$ and the arm's $\alpha'$:

- $\text{TV} = \tfrac12 \sum_j |\alpha_j - \alpha'_j|$, the largest change in the probability of
  any set of features (a credible set is one).
- $\text{KL}(\alpha \,\|\, \alpha') = \sum_j \alpha_j \log(\alpha_j / \alpha'_j)$, in nats,
  computed from log BFs (no floor). Large when the arm puts little mass where CAVI-Q2 has mass.
  It is the variable-selection term of the KL between the two single-effect posteriors.
- $\max_j |\alpha_j - \alpha'_j|$, the largest single-feature change (TV over single features).

At $L = 5$ the components are unordered, so each arm's components are matched to CAVI-Q2's by
minimum total TV. At both $L$, a component pair counts only if at least one side declares it
(component $\log \text{BF} \ge 2$); null components have diffuse $\alpha$ and their distances
are noise. The last table is per fit and needs no matching: $\max_j |\text{PIP}_j -
\text{PIP}'_j|$ over the combined PIPs. At $L = 1$ it equals $\max |\Delta\alpha|$ wherever a
component is declared.

Fits: 022 full grids (200 replicates), 023 and 024 full grids and `-ser` grids (200
replicates). Non-null cells only.

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
st = (fn.group_by("exp", "L", maintain_order=True)
      .agg(pl.col("batch_hash").n_unique().alias("batches"),
           (pl.len() / pl.col("method").n_unique()).cast(pl.Int64).alias("reps"),
           pl.col("n_pairs").mean().alias("pairs")).sort("exp", "L"))
for r in st.iter_rows(named=True):
    print(f"- {r['exp']}, L={r['L']}: {r['batches']} batches, {r['reps']} paired replicates per arm, "
          f"{r['pairs']:.2f} declared component pairs per fit")
```

```{python}
#| label: helpers

def table(df, value, legend, digits=3):
    tab = P.fmt(P.summarize(df, value, ["exp", "L", "method"]), digits)
    print(R.md_table(tab, rows=["exp", "L"], value="cell", fmt="{}", legend=legend))

COMMON = ("*exp*: experiment (022 binary Markov sets, 023 Gaussian AR(1), 024 nested sets). "
          "*L*: fitted components. Each arm column: mean over {unit}, with a 95% interval from "
          "resampling replicates. 0 = identical to CAVI-Q2.")
```


## Per replicate {#sec-per-rep}

A small mean distance can come from every replicate being close or from most replicates being
identical and a few far apart. To tell these apart, take one number per fit, $\max_j
|\text{PIP}_j - \text{PIP}'_j|$, the largest PIP change over all 256 features, and look at
its distribution over replicates. It needs no component matching.

```{python}
#| label: tab-pip-quantiles
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(R.md_table(P.quantile_cells(fn), rows=["exp", "L"], value="cell", fmt="{}",
      legend="*exp*: experiment (022 binary Markov sets, 023 Gaussian AR(1), 024 nested sets). "
             "*L*: fitted components. Each arm column: median / 90th / 99th percentile over fits "
             "(non-null cells, every replicate) of the largest absolute PIP difference from "
             "CAVI-Q2 on the same replicate."))
```

```{python}
#| label: tab-pip-shares
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(R.md_table(P.share_cells(fn), rows=["exp", "L"], value="cell", fmt="{}",
      legend="Columns as above. Each arm column: share of fits whose largest absolute PIP "
             "difference from CAVI-Q2 is at most 0.01 / above 0.1."))
```

### When gIBSS and CAVI-Q2 disagree {#sec-tail}

The fits in the tail are mostly different optima of the same objective. The table splits fits by
their largest PIP difference and compares the Q2 ELBO, which CAVI-Q2 maximizes directly, so a
small deficit for the gIBSS arms is expected even at the same optimum.

```{python}
#| label: tab-tail
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(P.md_frame(P.tail_table(fn), {"median ΔELBO": "{:+.3f}", "CAVI-Q2 higher": "{:.1%}",
                                    "arm higher": "{:.1%}", "declared count differs": "{:.1%}"},
      legend="*band*: the fit's largest absolute PIP difference from CAVI-Q2. *fits*: fits in the "
             "band (non-null cells). *median ΔELBO*: median of arm Q2 ELBO minus CAVI-Q2's, in "
             "nats. *CAVI-Q2 higher* / *arm higher*: share of fits where that side's ELBO is "
             "higher by more than 0.1 nat. *declared count differs*: share of fits where the two "
             "sides declare a different number of components (log BF >= 2)."))
```


### Why the PIPs differ {#sec-why}

For a fit in the tail, take the feature $j^*$ with the largest PIP difference. With the
components matched (minimum total TV), $\log(1-\text{PIP}_{j^*})$ is a sum over components,
so the gap splits exactly into one term per matched pair:

$$\log(1-\text{PIP}'_{j^*}) - \log(1-\text{PIP}_{j^*}) = \sum_l \left[\log(1-\alpha'_{s(l)j^*}) - \log(1-\alpha_{lj^*})\right].$$

The pair with the largest term drives the gap. It falls into one of five types by which side
declares it (component $\log\text{BF} \ge 2$):

- *same CS*: both sides declare it and $j^*$ is in both 95% credible sets, so the mass moved
  within a shared set.
- *CS moved*: both declare it but $j^*$ is in only one of the two sets.
- *CAVI-only* / *arm-only*: one side declares it. *near* means the other side's log BF is at
  least 1, within one unit of the threshold; *far* means below 1.
- *undeclared*: neither side declares it.

```{python}
#| label: tab-drivers
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
dt = P.driver_table(tf)
pct = {c: "{:.0%}" for c in dt.columns if c not in ("arm", "L", "fits")}
print(P.md_frame(dt, pct,
      legend="Fits with max |ΔPIP| > 0.1, non-null cells. *fits*: number of such fits. Type "
             "columns: share of fits whose PIP gap is driven by that pair type (they sum to 1). "
             "*driver explains*: median share of the summed |terms| that the driving pair "
             "carries. *CAVI-Q2 closer*: share of fits where CAVI-Q2's PIP at j\\* is closer "
             "to the truth (1 if j\\* is causal, else 0)."))
```

In most of the gIBSS tail, the driving pair is one neither side declares.

```{python}

       "α at j*, arm": "{:.2f}", "j* causal": "{:.0%}", "CAVI-Q2 PIP higher": "{:.0%}"},
      legend="Tail fits driven by an undeclared pair. *log BF*: median component log BF of "
             "the driving pair on each side. *α at j\\**: median alpha of that component at the "
             "worst feature. *j\\* causal*: share where the worst feature is causal. "
```

```{python}
      legend="gIBSS-Q2, L = 5, fits with max |ΔPIP| > 0.1: the most common counts of matched "
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-worst
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "The four L = 5 replicates with the largest gIBSS-Q2 PIP difference from CAVI-Q2. Left CAVI-Q2, right gIBSS-Q2, same replicate; coloured points are declared 95% credible sets, gIBSS-Q2 components coloured by their CAVI-Q2 match; ringed features with vertical lines are the causal features. x is cropped to the features with any PIP.
```
